svg.aria-label: Diagram of break-glass access. The normal path runs corporate identity provider, then IAM Identity Center, then a permission set, then the account. The break-glass path must share no link with it: an IAM user with its own MFA, held outside that chain, reaching the account directly. Below, two panels: split knowledge, where one group holds the password and another the MFA device, and separately one group holds the root email inbox and another the registered phone number; and loud by construction, where every use raises an alert through EventBridge and SNS and GuardDuty, because a break-glass credential that can be used quietly is an administrator credential. At the bottom, the circular storage trap: the credential must not be stored in a tool that depends on the account it recovers.
svg.title: Why the break-glass path must share no dependency with the normal one, and how it is split and alarmed
svg.text: Every dependency the normal path has, break-glass must not
A shared link is not a shortcut. It is the thing that will be broken on the day you reach for the glass.
Normal path — four dependencies, any one of which can be the outage
Corporate IdP
SAML or OIDC
IAM Identity Center
directory and sign-in
Permission set
assignment, still valid
The account
Break-glass path — must share none of them
IAM user, its own MFA, its own credentials
The one case AWS names for long-term credentials: you cannot reach the IdP.
direct, no intermediary
The account
Split the knowledge, twice
One group holds the password. A different group holds
the MFA device. One member of each must meet to sign in.
Then do it again for recovery: one group has the root email
inbox, another the registered phone. Both are verification
channels, so one person holding both is one person with root.
Loud by construction
A break-glass credential that can be used quietly is not a
break-glass credential. It is an administrator credential.
EventBridge on the sign-in event into SNS, a GuardDuty
finding for root usage, and a written procedure for the
person who receives the alert at 3am and must judge it.
The circular dependency, stated by AWS itself
Do not store the root password in a tool that depends on the account that password recovers. Lose the password, lose the tool that holds it.
Test the path on a schedule. A break-glass credential nobody has used is a credential nobody knows is broken.
